DASHBOARD UPGRADE SPECIFICATION
Student • Buddy • Admin
Version 1.0 | June 2026 | Internal Engineering Document
PURPOSE OF THIS DOCUMENT

This document is the complete engineering and design specification for upgrading the CareerRai dashboard MVP. It is written to be uploaded directly into Claude Code. Every feature is described with: what to build, exactly how it should look and behave, which database fields it needs, and why it exists. Build in sprint order. Do not skip sections.
THE ONE PRODUCT TRUTH (read before building anything)

A student must experience, within 7 days of joining, their IIM buddy saying something specific about their specific data. That proof-of-attention is what gets renewed. Every feature in this document exists to make that moment happen reliably, at scale, with minimum buddy effort.
HOW TO USE THIS DOCUMENT

This document is structured in three major sections — one per dashboard (Student, Buddy, Admin). Within each section, features are grouped into sprints. Build Sprint 1 before Sprint 2. Never skip a Sprint 1 feature to build a Sprint 2 feature.
SPRINT 1 — Must be live before the first paid student is onboarded
SPRINT 2 — Must be live by end of Month 1 (first 30 days of operation)
SPRINT 3 — Month 2 enhancements. Do not build these until Sprint 1 and 2 are tested and stable
Each feature specification follows this format:
What it is — one sentence
Why it exists — the exact student or buddy problem it solves
Exact UI/UX — pixel-level behavior, copy, states, and interactions
Database — which tables and fields it reads from or writes to
AI usage — if Anthropic Claude API is used, the exact prompt and output format
Design notes — color, animation, mobile behavior
SECTION 1
STUDENT DASHBOARD
Maximum engagement, minimum friction, one goal: student still logging at Day 30
1.1 ONBOARDING SEQUENCE — Day 1 (Sprint 1)
WHY THIS EXISTS

For a zero-brand startup, the first 10 minutes in the product are the only minutes where trust can be established before the student forms a judgment. The current dashboard drops students directly into the home page with no context. 60-70% will never return. This onboarding sequence fixes that.
Trigger: Fires once, on first login, for any new student account. Non-skippable. 4 screens. Progress indicator at top shows Screen 1/4, 2/4, 3/4, 4/4.
Screen 1: Meet Your Buddy
Full screen. CareerRai orange-tinted background (#FFF3EE). Center-aligned.
Top: Small CareerRai logo + 'Your Buddy is ready' in teal
Buddy card: Round avatar (120px), Buddy full name, IIM college badge (e.g., 'IIM Bangalore'), CAT percentile badge (e.g., '98.7%ile CAT 2024')
Below card: Audio player component — a large orange play button, waveform animation (CSS-only, simulated), duration counter
Audio file: Buddy records a 30-45 second personalized intro via the Buddy Dashboard (see Section 2.1). File stored in Supabase Storage. Path: buddy-intros/{buddy_id}.webm
If no audio uploaded yet: Show text fallback — buddy's written intro message from their profile
Button: 'Let’s Begin →' — only enabled after audio plays at least 10 seconds (or after 5 seconds if no audio)
DB: Read from profiles (buddy_id, full_name, college, cat_percentile, intro_audio_url). If buddy_id is null, show generic IIM Alumni card and skip audio.
Screen 2: Your Baseline Test
Heading: 'Your buddy needs this to guide you' — not 'Take a test'
Sub: 'Takes 5 minutes. 35 questions. Your score tells your buddy exactly where to focus with you.'
Large illustration / icon of diagnostic chart
If student has already completed CAT readiness test: Skip this screen automatically, show score summary instead
Button: 'Take the 5-Minute Test' — routes to /student/exams, opens test modal immediately
Button 2 (text link): 'I’ll do this later' — allowed but shows warning: 'Your buddy can’t give personalized guidance without this. Strongly recommended.'
DB: Check test_results table for student_id + test_type = 'cat-readiness'. If exists, skip.
Screen 3: Set Your Daily Commitment
Heading: 'One honest question'
Sub: 'How many hours can you realistically study on a typical weekday? Be honest — this becomes your streak target.'
Large number picker: 1 / 1.5 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5+ hours. Tap to select. Selected state: orange fill, white number.
Below picker: 'Your buddy will be notified if you consistently miss this target.'
This number is saved as study_target_hours in profiles table. Used for streak calculation and buddy alerts.
Button: 'This is my commitment'
DB: Update profiles.study_target_hours. Default 2 if skipped.
Screen 4: Log Day 1
Heading: 'Day 1. Streak starts now.'
Large animated flame icon (CSS: pulse animation, orange #E8652D, growing from small to normal over 1 second on screen enter)
Sub: 'Log today’s study session. Even 30 minutes counts. Your buddy sees every log.'
Simplified quick-log: Just 3 fields visible — Study Hours (slider), Topics (multi-select pills: Quant / VARC / LRDI / Mock / Revision), How did it go? (3 emoji options: 🙏 Tough / 💪 Solid / 🙊 Easy)
Button: 'Submit and Enter Dashboard'
On submit: Confetti animation (CSS), streak counter animates from 0 to 1, transition to /student/home
DB: Insert into daily_reports. Set streak to 1 in a new streak_data table (student_id, current_streak, longest_streak, last_log_date).
1.2 HOME PAGE REDESIGN (Sprint 1)
WHY THIS EXISTS

The current home page shows a greeting, quick stats, and a heatmap. None of these create emotional urgency to open the app tomorrow. The streak must be the first thing a student sees — not a stat buried below the fold. Research confirms: users with 7-day streaks retain at 2.4x the rate of users who never establish streaks.
Element 1: THE STREAK HERO (replaces heatmap as primary UI element)
Position: TOP of home page, above all other content. Full width card.
Background: Dark navy (#1A1A2E) card with orange flame icon (left) and streak number (right)
Flame states:
Day 1-6: Orange flame (🔥), medium size, no glow
Day 7-13: Orange flame, larger, subtle drop-shadow glow
Day 14+: Gold gradient flame (#FFD700 → #E8652D), larger, pulsing glow animation (CSS keyframes, 2s loop)
Broken streak: Grey flame (🩶), with text 'Streak broken. Start again today.'
Streak number: Large (48px), bold, white, next to flame. E.g., '14'
Sub-label: 'Day streak 🔥 Keep it alive' in orange. Or if broken: 'Streak lost. Your buddy has been notified.' in muted red
Below streak number: 'Your buddy checks your streak every Monday.' in small grey text — this line is crucial, makes the streak social not just personal
Right side: Small 'Log Today' button (pill shape, orange) if today's report not yet submitted
DB: Read streak_data table. Calculate: if last_log_date = yesterday or today, streak is active. If last_log_date < yesterday, streak is broken. Logic runs on page load.
DESIGN: No animation on first render. Flame pulse starts 1 second after page load to avoid jarring.
Element 2: BUDDY SIGNAL CARD (new, Sprint 1)
Position: Second card on home page, below streak
Shows the most recent buddy interaction: feedback note, voice note, or milestone message
If buddy has sent something in the last 7 days: Show a teal card with buddy avatar (small), buddy name, and a preview of the message (first 80 chars + 'Read more')
Tap to expand: Opens full buddy message / voice note player inline
If no buddy message in 7 days: Show: '🔔 Waiting for your buddy to review your week. Keep logging so they have data.' — this creates gentle pressure on the buddy without the student knowing
If buddy has left a voice note: Show audio waveform + play button inside the card. Duration shown. 'New' badge if unread.
DB: Read latest record from feedback table (student_id, created_at DESC). Check for voice_note_url. Mark as read on open.
Element 3: DAYS TO CAT CONTEXT CARD (new, Sprint 1)
Position: Third card
Shows: Exact days remaining until CAT exam (hardcoded CAT date: Nov 23, 2026, updated annually)
Shows dynamic contextual message based on days remaining:
180+ days: 'Foundation phase. Build habits now — they compound harder than any topic revision.'
90-180 days: 'Mock phase. One mock per week minimum. Your buddy is watching your scores closely.'
30-90 days: 'Final stretch. Don’t change strategy now. Your buddy will guide every mock.'
Under 30 days: 'Last mile. Trust your preparation. Your buddy has one job: keep you calm.'
Design: White card, teal left-border accent (4px), exam icon, days number in large bold orange
DB: No DB needed. CAT date hardcoded as constant. Days calculated client-side.
Element 4: QUICK STATS (keep, minor redesign)
Keep existing 4 stats (Avg Study/Day, Mock Tests, Confidence, Stress) but reduce visual prominence
Display as a 2x2 grid below the context card, not as the primary content
Add trend arrows (up/down/flat) with color: green = improving, red = declining, grey = flat
Element 5: HEATMAP (demote, keep)
Move heatmap to the Reports page as its primary home. Keep a mini 7-day version on home page only.
Label it: 'Last 7 Days' not '14-Day Heatmap'
This frees space for the streak hero and buddy signal card which are higher-retention features
Milestone Auto-Messages (Sprint 1 — critical)
On Day 7 streak: Auto-insert a record in feedback table from buddy to student with template message:
Message: '[Student first name], 7 days in a row. Most students don’t make it here. You’re already ahead of 60% of this batch. Keep it up. — [Buddy first name], [IIM name]'
Type: 'milestone_auto', not editable by buddy
This appears in the Buddy Signal Card on the student home page
On Day 21 streak: Same pattern, different message: '[Student], 3 weeks of consistency. This is where serious aspirants separate from the rest. Your CAT prep is on track. — [Buddy]'
Buddy receives an in-app alert: '[Student name] just hit their 7-day streak. Consider sending a personal voice note — this is the highest-impact moment for retention.'

DB: Implement via a background check (Next.js API route called on page load, or Supabase Edge Function triggered on daily_reports insert). Check streak_data.current_streak. If exactly 7 or 21 and no milestone message already sent (add milestone_sent_7 boolean to streak_data), insert feedback record.
1.3 DAILY LOG — FRICTION REDUCTION (Sprint 1)
WHY THIS EXISTS

Students stop logging because it takes too long. The current form has 10+ fields. Research shows: if a daily habit requires more than 60 seconds, abandonment climbs sharply after Week 2. We reduce to a 2-tap minimum path while keeping the data rich for buddy analysis.
Two-Mode Log: Quick Log vs Full Log
Quick Log (default, 2-tap minimum):
Field 1: Hours studied today — 5 large tap buttons: 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 / 4+
Field 2: Topics — pill buttons, multi-select: Quant / VARC / LRDI / Mock / Revision
Field 3: How did it go? — 3 emoji tap options: 🙏 Tough / 💪 Solid / 🙊 Easy (maps to confidence 1-2, 3-4, 5)
Submit button: 'Done — Log My Day' (large, full-width, orange)
Total time to complete: under 15 seconds
Full Log (expandable, optional):
A 'Tell me more' link expands to show: mock test details, exact confidence/stress sliders, sleep quality, notes field
Pre-fill anything that can be inferred: if 'Mock' topic selected, show mock fields automatically
The Quick Log data maps to existing daily_reports fields: study_duration, topics_covered, confidence (derived from emoji), stress (derived from emoji, inverted)
If student does Full Log, all existing fields are preserved as-is
DESIGN: Quick Log lives in a bottom sheet (slides up from bottom on mobile). Full width. High-contrast on dark overlay. 'X' to close without saving.
DB: No schema changes needed. Quick Log emoji maps: 🙏 = confidence:2, stress:4 | 💪 = confidence:4, stress:2 | 🙊 = confidence:5, stress:1. Sleep and nutrition default to null if not filled.
Streak Guard (Sprint 1)
If student has not logged by 9 PM (check on page load after 9 PM): Show a full-width amber banner at top of every page: '🔔 Log today before midnight to keep your [X]-day streak. Takes 15 seconds.'
Tap banner → opens Quick Log bottom sheet directly
This is NOT a push notification (requires no setup). It is an in-app UI state that checks on every page load after 9 PM.
IMPLEMENTATION: In a shared layout component, check: today's date vs last_log_date. If different and time > 21:00 local, show banner. Use client-side time.
1.4 MOCK SCORE DROP INTERVENTION (Sprint 1)
WHY THIS EXISTS

The October crash is the #1 churn event. Students see their percentile drop 20-30 points in October, panic, and cancel. This feature contextualizes the drop before panic sets in, and automatically flags the buddy.
Drop Detection Logic
When a student submits a daily report with mock_taken = true and a mock score:
Calculate: current_percentile vs previous_mock_percentile (stored in test_results or computed from mock scores)
If drop > 8 percentile points: trigger the intervention UI
Also triggered if student takes the CAT Readiness Test and scores 10+ points lower than their previous attempt
Intervention UI
After score submission: Before showing the results/confirmation, show a full-screen overlay card:
Title: 'Score drop detected. This is expected. Here’s why.'

Brief explanation (2 sentences): 'As CAT gets closer, more serious competitors take mocks. The pool gets tougher, so the same accuracy gives a lower percentile. Your skill hasn’t declined — the benchmark moved.'
Simple visual: 2-column comparison — 'May pool: All aspirants' vs 'October pool: Only serious aspirants'
Message: 'Your buddy has been flagged about this drop. Expect a message from them within 24 hours.'
Button: 'Got it. Show my score.'
This message fires maximum once per student per 30-day period to avoid over-triggering
DB: Create a mock_drop_alerts table: student_id, triggered_at, buddy_notified (boolean). Check before triggering.
BUDDY ALERT: When triggered, insert a high-urgency flag into the buddy's triage system (see Section 2). Urgency reason: 'Mock score dropped [X] points. Student needs context and encouragement.
1.5 CAT READINESS TEST — RESULT SCREEN ENHANCEMENT (Sprint 2)
WHY THIS EXISTS

The test result screen is the highest emotional moment in the student journey. It determines whether the student feels hopeful or hopeless. Currently the screen is analytically solid but emotionally inert. These enhancements turn it into a retention moment.
Addition 1: AI-Generated Buddy-Style Insight (Claude API)
After displaying the score and category breakdown, add a section: 'What your buddy would say about this score'
This section calls the Claude API with the student's scores, category breakdown, and exam timeline to generate a 3-4 sentence personalized insight
API call parameters:
Model: claude-sonnet-4-20250514

System prompt: 'You are an IIM alumni buddy reviewing a CAT aspirant’s readiness test score. Your tone is direct, warm, like a senior bhaiya. Write 3 sentences: (1) one honest observation about their strongest category, (2) one honest observation about their weakest category, (3) one specific action they should take this week. Use first-person as the buddy. No generic advice. Be specific to their numbers. Max 80 words.'
User message: 'Student score: [X]/100. Percentile: [Y]%. Category breakdown: Quant [a]%, VARC [b]%, LRDI [c]%, Mock Strategy [d]%, Wellness [e]%. Days to CAT: [n].'
Display the AI output in a teal-bordered card with buddy avatar placeholder and label: 'Buddy’s Take (AI-generated)'
Add small disclaimer: '★ Based on your scores. Your real buddy will review this too.'
API: Use fetch to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages. No API key needed in client (route through a Next.js API route at /api/buddy-insight). Cache result by test attempt ID to avoid repeat calls.
Addition 2: Comparison Anchor
Add a single comparison line below the percentile: 'Students at your percentile need an average of [X] additional mocks to reach 90+ percentile.'
This creates urgency without being demoralizing — it frames the gap as solvable with a known action
Values are hardcoded lookup table based on percentile bands (no DB needed)
1.6 STUDENT-BUDDY SHARED TIMELINE (Sprint 2)
WHY THIS EXISTS

The relationship must be visible to the student. When a student can scroll through a feed of: 'Day 7 — Buddy sent voice note', 'Day 12 — You hit 85th percentile', 'Day 15 — Buddy left feedback', they feel the relationship is real and ongoing. This is the single biggest perceived-value driver.
New Page: /student/journey
A reverse-chronological feed. Add 'Journey' to bottom navigation (replace 'Profile' in nav; Profile accessible via settings icon top-right)
Each feed item is a card. Item types:
🔥 Study Log — 'You studied [X] hrs — [topics]. Streak day [N].' — tappable to expand full log
🎯 Test Score — 'CAT Readiness: [score]/100, [percentile]%ile' — tappable to see full result
🎤 Voice Note from Buddy — '[Buddy name] sent you a voice note' — tap to play inline audio player
📝 Buddy Feedback — Preview of written feedback, tap to expand
🏆 Milestone — '7-day streak achieved!', '90th percentile reached!' etc.
Grouped by week: 'This Week', 'Last Week', '[Month] Week 2', etc.
Empty state (first login): 'Your journey starts today. Every log, every buddy message, every milestone will appear here.'
DB: This is a view/query combining daily_reports, test_results, feedback tables ordered by created_at DESC. No new table needed.
DESIGN: Clean white cards, color-coded left border by type (orange=log, teal=buddy, gold=milestone). Mobile-first. Infinite scroll.

Buddy Credential Display (upgrade existing)
Current: Shows buddy name + 'Connected' badge. Upgrade to show full buddy credential card:

SECTION 2
BUDDY DASHBOARD
Maximum impact, minimum time. Under 5 minutes per student per week — non-negotiable.
THE BUDDY CONSTRAINT

Buddies are part-time IIM alumni. They are NOT full-time employees. If the dashboard requires 20+ minutes per student, buddies will quit. Every feature here is designed around one constraint: 5 minutes per student per week. The dashboard tells the buddy WHAT TO DO, not just shows them data.
2.1 BUDDY ONBOARDING — Intro Audio Recording (Sprint 1)
WHY THIS EXISTS
The student's Day 1 onboarding (Section 1.1) requires a buddy audio intro. The buddy must be able to record and upload this before any students are assigned. This is a 2-minute setup, one time.
New Page: /buddy/setup (shown on first login if intro not recorded)
Title: 'Record Your Intro Message'
Instructions: 'Your students hear this on Day 1. Keep it under 45 seconds. Say: your name, your IIM, your CAT score, and one thing you wish you’d known when you were preparing.'
Record button (large, red ● when recording): Uses browser MediaRecorder API. No external service.
Waveform visualization during recording (CSS animation, bars moving)
Playback before saving. Re-record option.
Save button: Uploads to Supabase Storage bucket 'buddy-intros/{buddy_id}.webm'. Updates profiles.intro_audio_url.
Also on this page: Buddy can write a 1-sentence bio: 'I scored X%ile on my Nth attempt. Here’s what I’d tell my past self…' — stored in profiles.buddy_bio
TECH: MediaRecorder API supported in all modern browsers. Record as audio/webm. Max file size ~2MB for 45s. Supabase Storage handles this without any paid tier at this volume.
2.2 HOME PAGE — THE TRIAGE VIEW (Sprint 1)
WHY THIS EXISTS

The current buddy home shows an alphabetical student list. A buddy with 8 students spends 10 minutes figuring out who needs attention. The triage view shows who needs help in 30 seconds, ranked by urgency. This is the single biggest buddy experience improvement.
Urgency Score Algorithm
Each student receives an urgency score (0-100) calculated on page load. Higher = needs attention more urgently.
Days since last log: 0 days = 0 pts, 1 day = 10 pts, 2 days = 25 pts, 3+ days = 45 pts (max contribution 45)
Stress trend (last 3 days avg): below 3 = 0 pts, 3-4 = 10 pts, above 4 = 20 pts (max 20)
Mock score drop flag active: +20 pts
Days since buddy last gave ANY feedback/interaction: 0-3 days = 0 pts, 4-7 days = 10 pts, 7+ days = 15 pts (max 15)
Total max: 100. Thresholds: 0-30 = Green (On Track), 31-60 = Amber (Monitor), 61+ = Red (Needs Attention)
Triage Cards Layout
Page title: 'Your Students' with subtitle showing: 'X need attention • Y to monitor • Z on track'
Red (Needs Attention) cards always shown first, then Amber, then Green
Each card (full-width, mobile):
Left: Round avatar with colored border (red/amber/green)
Center: Student name (bold), urgency reason in small text (e.g., '3 days no log + stress rising')
Right: Three action buttons (icon-only on mobile, icon+label on desktop):
🎤 Voice (opens voice recorder)
💬 Message (opens text message input)
📝 Feedback (opens full feedback form)
Tapping student name opens student detail page
Green cards: Collapsed by default into a 'X students on track — tap to see' section at bottom

DB: Query joins daily_reports (latest per student), feedback (latest per student), streak_data, and mock_drop_alerts. Urgency score calculated in JavaScript on the client from fetched data. No stored urgency score — always computed fresh.
2.3 VOICE NOTE FEATURE (Sprint 2 — highest priority in Sprint 2)
WHY THIS EXISTS

Research confirms: students are significantly more likely to retain information from audio than text. A voice note from an IIM alumni addressing the student by name, referencing their specific data, is the single highest-impact interaction in the entire product. Text feedback feels automated. A voice feels human. This is what students will tell friends about.
Voice Note Recorder
Accessible from: (1) Triage card quick-action button, (2) Student detail page top action bar
Opens as a bottom sheet (slides up)
UI: Large red record button (●). Waveform animation while recording. Timer showing seconds elapsed.
Hard limit: 90 seconds. Counter shows '0:45 / 1:30'. At 1:20 a warning appears: '10 seconds remaining'.
After recording: Playback option. 'Send' button or 'Re-record' button.
On Send: Upload to Supabase Storage at 'voice-notes/{student_id}/{timestamp}.webm'. Insert record in feedback table with voice_note_url populated, feedback_text = null.
Student receives in-app notification: '🎤 [Buddy name] sent you a voice note.' (see notification system, Section 2.6)
TECH: Same MediaRecorder approach as buddy intro. Supabase Storage. Browser-native, no external service. Test cross-browser: Chrome Android, Safari iOS, Chrome desktop. File size: ~1MB per minute.

DESIGN: The record button should feel weighty and satisfying. Use a box-shadow pulse animation while recording to signal 'this is live'. The 90-second limit is intentional — longer notes take too long for students to listen to and too long for buddies to record.
2.4 WEEKLY SIGNAL — AUTO-GENERATED SUMMARY (Sprint 2)
WHY THIS EXISTS

Every Monday, each buddy should review each student. Without a pre-built summary, this requires reading 7 days of raw logs. That takes 5+ minutes per student. With the Weekly Signal, it takes 90 seconds. This is the feature that makes the 5-minute-per-student constraint achievable.
Weekly Signal Card
Shown prominently on the Student Detail page, at the top, every Monday (and persists until buddy acts on it)
Four data points displayed as a 2x2 grid of mini-stats:
Days logged / 7 (e.g., '5/7 days')
Avg hours/day (e.g., '2.3 hrs/day')
Stress trend: arrow up/down/flat with color coding
Latest mock performance (or 'No mock this week')
Below the grid: ONE AI-generated insight sentence (Claude API):

System prompt: 'You are reviewing a CAT student’s week of data. Give one precise observation (max 20 words) that a mentor should act on. No generic advice. Focus on the most unusual or concerning pattern.'
Input: The student's 7-day log summary data as JSON
Output: Single sentence, e.g., 'Stress spiked Thursday-Friday but study hours stayed high — likely mock anxiety after a poor result.'
Below insight: THREE action buttons (same as triage):
🎤 Send voice note
Keep Going (sends auto milestone message)
📝 Write feedback
After buddy takes action: The Weekly Signal card collapses and shows 'Reviewed this week ✔' in green
DB: Weekly Signal data pulled fresh from daily_reports for last 7 days. AI insight generated via /api/weekly-insight Next.js route. Cache by student_id + week_start to avoid redundant API calls.
2.5 STUDENT DETAIL PAGE — REDESIGN (Sprint 2)
Layout: Three sections, clean separation
Section A: Weekly Signal (described above) — collapses after action

Section B: The Relationship Timeline — same feed as student sees in /student/journey, but from buddy POV. Buddy can see all their own previous messages, voice notes, and student's logs in chronological order. This replaces the '30 report list' in the current MVP.
Section C: Test History — keep existing. Add simple bar chart showing CAT Readiness score over time (Recharts BarChart, max 5 bars, orange color).
Quick Stats Header (keep, minor improvements)
Keep existing student info header
Add: 'Last active: [X] days ago' in a small badge — makes inactivity immediately visible
Add: Current streak number next to name — e.g., '🔥 14-day streak'
Feedback Form (improve existing)
Keep existing form structure
Add: AI-draft assistant. A small 'Draft with AI' button below the feedback textarea.
Calls Claude API with student's last week data and previous feedback given
Generates a 3-sentence feedback draft in buddy's voice
Buddy edits and personalizes before sending
This reduces the effort of writing feedback from 5 minutes to 2 minutes

System prompt: 'You are an IIM alumni writing feedback for a CAT student. Use direct, warm, senior-bhaiya tone. 3 sentences: observation on consistency, observation on weak area, one specific action for this week. Max 60 words.'
AI BUDGET NOTE: These API calls are cheap (< ₹0.01 per call). At 10 buddies × 10 students × 4 weeks = 400 calls/month. Negligible cost.
2.6 NOTIFICATION SYSTEM (Sprint 2)
WHY THIS EXISTS

Currently there is no way to notify buddies when students need attention, or to notify students when buddies respond. Without this, the relationship is asynchronous but invisible. A buddy could respond and the student might not see it for 3 days.
In-App Notification Bell (not email, not push)
Add a bell icon (🔔) to the top navigation bar of both student and buddy dashboards
Red badge count when unread notifications exist
Notification types for STUDENTS:
🎤 '[Buddy name] sent you a voice note' — triggered on voice note upload
📝 '[Buddy name] left you feedback' — triggered on feedback insert
🏆 'Streak milestone: 7 days! Message from your buddy waiting.' — triggered on milestone
⚠️ 'Log today before midnight to keep your [X]-day streak' — shown after 9 PM
Notification types for BUDDIES:
⚠️ '[Student name] hasn’t logged in 2 days' — triggered by urgency score crossing 60
📉 '[Student name]’s mock score dropped significantly' — triggered by mock drop alert
🏆 '[Student name] hit their 7-day streak! Great time for a voice note.'
Notifications page (/student/notifications and /buddy/notifications): Simple list, reverse chronological, tap to navigate to relevant item

DB: Create notifications table: id, user_id, type, title, message, link_url, read_at (nullable), created_at. Insert via Supabase server-side triggers or Next.js API routes at the point of each triggering event.
2.7 BUDDY TRENDS PAGE — SIMPLIFY (Sprint 3)
Current trends page has complex multi-student comparison charts. For 10 students, this is useful. For 5 students (early stage), it’s overkill.
Sprint 3 action: Keep the page but replace multi-chart complexity with one simple table: Student Name / Streak / Stress Trend / Last Mock / Last Feedback Given / Status Badge (Red/Amber/Green)
This table tells the buddy everything they need in one glance. No chart reading required.
SECTION 3
ADMIN DASHBOARD
Nishant's operational control panel. Speed over beauty. Function over form.
ADMIN PHILOSOPHY

The admin dashboard is not a product. It is a founder's cockpit. Nishant has 2-3 hours per day maximum. The admin dashboard must surface critical information in under 60 seconds and allow bulk actions without manual record-by-record editing.
3.1 HOME PAGE — NORTH STAR METRICS (Sprint 1)
WHY THIS EXISTS
The current admin home shows generic KPIs. What Nishant needs to see every day are the three metrics that determine if the business is alive: Day 30 retention, buddy response rate, and renewal risk.
Replace existing KPI cards with these 5:
KPI 1: ACTIVE STUDENTS (logging at least 3x/week) — shown as X / Total enrolled. Color: Green if >70%, Amber if 50-70%, Red if <50%
KPI 2: BUDDY RESPONSE RATE (within 48 hrs) — % of student logs that received buddy interaction within 48 hours. Target: >90%. Color coded same as above.
KPI 3: AT-RISK STUDENTS — Count of students with urgency score > 60 AND no buddy response in 72+ hours. This is the churn pipeline. Tapping this card shows the list.
KPI 4: TOTAL ACTIVE STREAKS — Students currently on a 7+ day streak. Leading indicator of Day 30 retention.

SECTION 5
AI INTEGRATION SPECIFICATION
All Claude API usage: prompts, routes, caching, cost
AI PRINCIPLES
AI is used in exactly 3 places. Never as a replacement for the buddy. Always as a draft or context tool that a human reviews. The student must always know when they are reading AI-generated content.
5.1 AI Use Case 1: CAT Test Buddy Insight
Route: POST /api/buddy-insight
Trigger: Student completes CAT Readiness Test, clicks 'Save & Continue'
Input: score (0-100), percentile (0-100), category_breakdown (JSON), days_to_cat (integer)
Output: 3-4 sentences. Displayed in teal card on result screen labeled 'Buddy’s Take (AI-generated)'
Caching: Cache by attempt_id in test_results table. Re-use cached response if student views result again. Never re-call API for same attempt.
PROMPT:
System: You are an IIM alumni buddy reviewing a CAT aspirant's readiness test. Tone: direct, warm, like a senior friend (bhaiya/didi). Write exactly 3 sentences:
1. One honest observation about their STRONGEST category (be specific about the number)
2. One honest observation about their WEAKEST category with one specific action
3. One motivational sentence tied to their days remaining to CAT. Max 80 words total. No generic phrases like 'keep working hard'.
5.2 AI Use Case 2: Weekly Signal Insight
Route: POST /api/weekly-insight
Trigger: Buddy opens Student Detail page on Monday (or the first time they open it during a given week)
Input: student_id, 7-day aggregated log data as JSON
Output: Single sentence insight (max 20 words). Displayed in Weekly Signal card above buddy action buttons.
Caching: Cache by student_id + week_start_date. Clear cache next Monday.
5.3 AI Use Case 3: Feedback Draft Assistant
Route: POST /api/feedback-draft
Trigger: Buddy clicks 'Draft with AI' inside feedback form
Input: student's last 7 days of log data, student's current streak, most recent test score, previous feedback given
Output: 2-3 sentence feedback draft. Inserted into textarea for buddy to edit.
No caching: Always generate fresh. Buddy edits before sending. AI output is a starting point, not final.
Label in UI: 'AI Draft — please personalize before sending'. Buddy cannot send without at least deleting/modifying the AI draft marker.

7.2 Animation Rules
Flame pulse: CSS keyframes. Scale 1.0 → 1.05 → 1.0 over 2 seconds, infinite. Only on streaks 14+.
Streak number increment: Count-up animation (0 to N over 600ms) on page load. Use a simple setInterval.
Card entrance: fade-in + translateY(8px → 0) over 300ms on page load. Apply to all cards with 50ms stagger.
Voice note waveform (recording): CSS bars animation. 5 bars, alternating heights, 0.6s cycle. Orange color.
Confetti (Day 1 log submit + milestone): CSS-only. 20 absolutely-positioned divs, random colors from brand palette, fall animation 1s, then disappear.
Bottom sheet: translateY(100% → 0) over 250ms with cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1). Standard iOS-feel spring.
NO page-level skeleton loaders on mobile — they feel slow. Use opacity fade-in on data arrival instead.
7.3 Mobile-First Rules
All tap targets: minimum 48x48px — this is non-negotiable for thumb usability
Bottom navigation: keep existing 4 items. Add 'Journey' by replacing 'Profile' (Profile accessible via top-right avatar).
Voice recorder bottom sheet: Full-width on mobile (100vw), centered fixed width (480px) on desktop.
Streak hero card: Full-width card on mobile. On desktop: part of a 2-column layout (streak left, buddy signal right).
Font sizes: Headlines 24px minimum on mobile. Body 16px minimum. Never go smaller for key information.
Quick Log bottom sheet: min-height 60vh on mobile so it feels substantial but leaves context visible above.
SECTION 8
WHAT NOT TO BUILD
Scope constraints. Say no to everything not in Sprints 1-3.
THE RULE

Every feature request that arrives during development must be evaluated: does it make the student more likely to log tomorrow AND renew next month? If not, it goes on a backlog list and is not discussed until Sprint 3 is complete.
Do NOT build in the next 3 months:
In-app chat / messaging between student and buddy (WhatsApp is sufficient and already trusted)
Group features / study groups / peer comparison (dilutes the 1:1 model and the product promise)
AI-generated study plans (we don't have enough longitudinal data yet; premature AI plans are worse than no plans)
Email notification system (In-app notifications + WhatsApp is sufficient at this stage; email requires deliverability setup)
iOS app (Android PWA or web first; iOS is Sprint 4+)
Payment integration inside dashboard (use Razorpay link + manual onboarding; this is Month 3+ feature)
Leaderboards or public student ranking (creates anxiety, not motivation, in high-stakes exam context)
Video calls (scope creep; the product promise is async buddy support, not synchronous coaching)
Student-to-student community (contradicts the 'personalized 1:1' positioning that justifies the price)
FINAL NOTE TO CLAUDE CODE
READ THIS BEFORE WRITING A SINGLE LINE OF CODE

You are building a product for students who chose to self-study instead of paying ₹50,000 for coaching. They made a hard, lonely decision. Everything in this dashboard exists to make them feel less alone. The streak tells them their effort is being counted. The buddy signal tells them someone is watching. The voice note tells them someone cares enough to speak their name. Build every feature as if a 23-year-old in a tier-2 city is logging their CAT prep at 11 PM and their only support system is this app and the IIM alumni on the other side of it. Build it that well.
